stem: A 19-year-old girl presented to the outpatient department complaining of left breast mass for 4 months. Examination revealed a well circumscribed, firm, smooth mobile lump, 3 x 4 cm in size in the lateral upper quadrant of the left breast. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
expl: A young woman with a well-circumscribed, firm, smooth, mobile ("breast mouse") lump = fibroadenoma, the commonest breast mass under 30.

stem: A 30-year-old female presents with breast pain that is cyclical, often worsening before her menstrual period. On examination, her breasts are lumpy and nodular, but there are no discrete, well-defined masses. What is the most likely diagnosis?
expl: Cyclical premenstrual pain with diffusely lumpy, nodular breasts and no discrete mass = fibrocystic changes.

why.D: A discrete hard mass; pain is not typical.

stem: A 17-year-old girl presents with a painless, mobile, well-circumscribed breast mass measuring 4 cm. Ultrasound shows a solid, well-defined lesion. What is the best management?
expl: A young girl with a typical, imaging-concordant fibroadenoma can be followed clinically and with ultrasound; excision is for size >3–4 cm with growth, symptoms or uncertainty (this key chose follow-up).

why.A: Not needed immediately for a typical lesion.

stem: A 40 year old patient presented with a 4.5 cm breast mass, biopsy showed that it was a phyllodes tumor. What is the appropriate management?

opts.t: Lumpectomy (wide local excision) with ≥1 cm margin
Lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node excision

expl: Phyllodes tumours are excised with a clear margin (≥1 cm). They rarely spread to lymph nodes, so no sentinel biopsy; enucleation alone has high recurrence; mastectomy only if a clear margin can't be obtained.

stem: A 45-year-old postpartum woman presented complaining of left breast pain associated with fever for one day. Her breast was erythematous and tender but not fluctuant. Breast ultrasound was normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
expl: Lactational mastitis (fever, erythema, tenderness, no collection on US) → continue breastfeeding/emptying the breast + anti-staphylococcal antibiotics. Stopping feeding causes stasis.

why.D: Inadequate once fever and infection are present.

stem: A 28 year old female with a bloody right nipple discharge for 2 weeks. On examination, no palpable breast mass. Breast ultrasound was normal.Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
expl: Bloody nipple discharge in a young woman with no mass and normal imaging → intraductal papilloma (commonest cause); cancer still excluded by triple assessment.

why.C: Usually older, with a mass/imaging finding.

stem: A 25 year old lady came to the clinic with history can of headache and visual changes with bilateral milky nipple discharge what is the best next investigation that needs to be done for the patient
expl: Headache, visual-field changes and bilateral galactorrhoea suggest a prolactinoma → check serum prolactin (and TSH, since hypothyroidism raises prolactin), then pituitary MRI.

why.A: Not the cause of bilateral milky discharge.
why.C: MRI pituitary comes after the hormone tests.

stem: Female came to the ER with Recurrent breast cellulitis 5 times with no improvement with multiple antibiotics. What is the next best management?
expl: "Cellulitis" that keeps recurring despite antibiotics must be biopsied to exclude inflammatory breast cancer (dermal lymphatic invasion).

stem: A 45-year-old lactating woman presented complaining of right breast pain associated with fever for one day. Breast ultrasound was normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
expl: Lactating woman with breast pain and fever for one day and a normal US (no collection) = lactational mastitis.

why.D: Not acute with fever in 1 day; consider only if it fails to resolve.

stem: Duct ectasia (I think they were asking about it’s features):

opts.t: Can present with greenish or whitish nipple discharge

srcNote: Source note (Final 439 A Q25): The source asks about the type of discharge in duct ectasia and states: Answer: A (Benign Breast Disorders). Original choice A: Mixed.
expl: Duct ectasia (dilated subareolar ducts, older women) can present with green/whitish/multicoloured thick discharge; it is benign and doesn't need surgery unless symptomatic. (A source note for another version wrote A.)

why.B: Periductal mastitis can coexist, but C is keyed.

stem: 10 year old boy presented with gynecomastisa, no palpable mass, no symptoms, ultrasound showed normal breast, management?
expl: Pubertal gynaecomastia in a boy with no mass and normal US is physiological and usually regresses → reassure and follow up.

why.B: Not in a child with physiological change.

stem: What is the type of nipple discharge in a female with duct ectasia?
srcNote: (Benign Breast Disorders) One or more answer choices are blank in the source.
expl: Duct ectasia gives thick, multicoloured ("mixed" — green, brown, white) discharge from several ducts.

stem: “Patient with phylloide tumor” what is the management?
srcNote: No answer key is stated in this source version.
expl: Phyllodes tumour → wide local excision (lumpectomy) with ≥1 cm clear margin; no sentinel node biopsy (nodal spread is rare).

why.B: Only if clear margins can't be obtained.

stem: A 50 year old woman complained of bilateral upper quadrant breast pain and tenderness. Which of the following is the modality of choice?
srcNote: (Benign Breast Disorders) Other source key (Final 432 A Q59 (p. 211)): Answer: C (Benign Breast diseases). Original choice C: Mammogram. This version does not offer a combined ultrasound-and-mammogram option.
expl: Women ≥40 with breast symptoms get mammogram + ultrasound (complementary). MRI is for high-risk screening or extent of known cancer. (432 version keyed mammogram alone.)

stem: A 47-year-old woman presented to the outpatient department complaining of nipple retraction and multiple discharges. On examination, no palpable breast mass. Breast ultrasound shows intraductal dilation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
expl: Nipple retraction with multi-duct discharge, no mass, and dilated ducts on US in a 47-year-old = duct ectasia.

stem: A 55 year old female complained of unilateral breast mass in the right breast. Physical examination shows a 4x4 cm mass in the upper quadrant of the right breast. What is your investigation of choice?
expl: A palpable mass in a woman >40 → diagnostic mammogram (with ultrasound) is the imaging of choice.

why.C: For high risk or extent of known cancer.

stem: A 47 year old female complains of bilateral breast pain with tenderness on the upper outer quadrant of both breasts. They ordered a mammogram for her, what is the reason for ordering a mammogram?

opts.t: Mammogram can show details of the mass

expl: Mammography's key strength is showing microcalcifications (and their type) and architectural distortion — early signs of cancer/DCIS.

why.D: US/MRI characterise masses better in dense breasts.

stem: A 28 year old female complains of unilateral bloody discharge from the right breast. Which of the following investigations will you order for her?
expl: A young woman (dense breasts) with bloody discharge → ultrasound first (retroareolar papilloma), then biopsy if needed.

stem: A 47-year-old female presenting to your clinic with a recent history of palpable breast mass, 3 cm in size. What is the next step in managing this patient after obtaining history and physical examination?

opts.t: Breast imaging followed by biopsy from the mass
Surgical removal of this mass and sending it for histopathology

expl: Triple assessment: history/exam → imaging (mammogram ± US) → image-guided core biopsy. Imaging comes before biopsy so the biopsy doesn't distort the images and is targeted.

why.D: Excision isn't the first diagnostic step.

stem: A 34-year-old female complains of left breast pain with a mass that increased in size for the last 3 months. Breast ultrasound showed a 4 cm simple cyst.What is the best management for this patient?

opts.t: Cyst aspiration and send fluid for cytology

expl: Source key D. A painful 4 cm simple cyst is aspirated. The doctor's notes say routine cytology of uncomplicated cyst fluid is not useful (only bloody fluid, a residual mass or recurrence needs further work-up) — recognise the key, but follow the doctor in practice.

why.A: A symptomatic cyst should be aspirated.
why.C: Excision is not needed for a simple cyst.

stem: A25-year-old girl presented with a palpable breast mass. Ultrasound showed that the size is 4 cm. Core biopsy proved that it is a fibroadenoma. What is the acceptable management?

opts.t: Antibiotics and follow up Ans. Both A&B were considered correct.

expl: The source says both A and B were considered correct: a core-proven 4 cm fibroadenoma in a 25-year-old may be followed (if stable, concordant) or excised (size >3–4 cm). Mastectomy and antibiotics are wrong.

stem: A 26-year-old lady who was involved in a car accident 5 months ago was referred to the clinic with right painless breast mass. There is 3x2 cm irregular mass by physical examination of her right breast. Her physician advised her to have ultrasound guided true cut biopsy. What is the most probable diagnosis?
expl: An irregular, painless mass months after breast trauma = fat necrosis (can mimic cancer clinically and on imaging; biopsy confirms).

why.D: Must be excluded, but the trauma history points to fat necrosis.

stem: A 25-year-old woman postpartum who is breastfeeding, presented to the ER with a complaint of pain in her right breast for 24 hours. Examination for the breast revealed swelling with skin redness in the lateral lower quadrant of the right breast with skin hotness and tenderness but no fluctuation. Blood pressure 115/75 mmHg. Heart rate 76 /min. Temperature 37. Which of the following is the most appropriate antibiotics in the treatment of this patient?
expl: Lactational mastitis is usually Staphylococcus aureus → flucloxacillin (dicloxacillin); cephalexin or clindamycin if penicillin-allergic.

stem: Patient with 5 cm fibroadenoma what will be her management ?

opts.t: refer her to a plastic surgeon

expl: Fibroadenomas >3–4 cm (here 5 cm), growing or symptomatic are excised (also to exclude phyllodes).

stem: A 43 year old female diagnosed to have fibrocystic changes in both breasts What will be her ultrasound findings?
expl: Fibrocystic change on ultrasound = multiple cysts of variable size within dense nodular tissue.

stem: 35 Y/O female postpartum lactating presented with red hot tender mass around the areola. Tx of choice:
srcNote: Source key was A; corrected — see explanation.
expl: Periareolar red, hot, tender mass in a lactating woman = mastitis/early abscess due to Staphylococcus aureus → flucloxacillin (as keyed in the other versions of this question). The 427 recall keyed ampicillin, which staphylococcal β-lactamase destroys.

why.A: Source key, but not effective against penicillinase-producing S. aureus.

stem: Fibroadenoma:
srcNote: not completed Q Incomplete recall; only the available options are reproduced.
expl: The question is incomplete in the source; the facts above are what was being tested.
ansText: Both listed statements are false: fibroadenomas are usually <3–5 cm (giant >5 cm is uncommon) and they are well encapsulated, mobile ("breast mouse").
